tasks.entryDescription: Remove edges/faces inductively in a planar graph; triangulate and count incidences; topological Euler characteristic.
tasks.routeTitle: Remove edges/faces inductively in a planar graph
tasks.currentSketch: Induct on the number F of faces of a connected planar graph. If F=1, the graph has no cycle and is a tree, so E=V−1 and V−E+F=2. Otherwise choose an edge incident to two distinct faces and delete it. The graph stays connected, while E and F each decrease by one; therefore V−E+F is unchanged. Induction proves the formula.

tasks.entryDescription: Remove edges/faces inductively in a planar graph; triangulate and count incidences; topological Euler characteristic.
tasks.currentSketch: View a convex polyhedron's boundary as a cell decomposition of the sphere. The Euler characteristic of S² is 2, and its cell count is V−E+F; hence the formula. This is topological and requires the surface be sphere-like (genus zero).

tasks.entryDescription: Cantor diagonal construction; nested intervals avoiding a proposed enumeration; cardinality via binary sequences.
tasks.currentSketch: Given any proposed list x₁,x₂,… of infinite binary sequences, form y by choosing yₙ≠(xₙ)ₙ. Then y differs from every listed sequence at its nth coordinate, so no enumeration is complete; Cantor's diagonal proves uncountability of {0,1}^N and hence R.

tasks.routeTitle: topology: winding number/fundamental group or degree
tasks.currentSketch: Let f(z)=P(z)/zⁿ on a large circle; by the argument principle the winding number of P(z) around 0 equals n for sufficiently large radius (dominant leading term). If P had no zero inside, its boundary winding number would be 0, contradiction. Rouché's theorem formalizes this comparison.

tasks.currentSketch: A nonconstant complex polynomial has |P(z)|→∞ as |z|→∞, so |P| attains a global minimum. If the minimum at z₀ were nonzero, write P(z₀+w)=a₀+aₖwᵏ+… with first nonzero k≥1. Choose w so aₖwᵏ/a₀ is small negative real; higher terms are lower order, making |P(z₀+w)|<|a₀|, contradiction.

tasks.currentSketch: For G(t)=∫ₐᵗf(x)dx, the difference quotient is the average value of f over [t,t+h]; continuity makes it tend to f(t), so G′=f. If F′=f, then (F−G)′=0, so F−G is constant and ∫ₐᵇf=F(b)−F(a).
